title: Compton's Pictured Encyclopedia
edition: 1st edition, c1922, 7 article volumes + Volume 8 reference section
corrections_note: Counted fixes (engine + context + proofread + headword): 34,936 (engine 33,006; context 912; proofread 739; headword 279). Structure/assembly operations are counted separately per volume and are not summed here; see corrections.md in the reference folder for the full per-volume lists.
source: HathiTrust record 100645814; Internet Archive first-edition scans comptonspictured01unse-08unse (F. E. Compton & Co., Chicago, 1922). Editor-in-Chief Guy Stanton Ford; Managing Editors Samuel Bannister Harding and Athol Ewart Rollins; Art Editor Seymour Jones. All 8 title pages read as images (copyright 1922, deposit stamp Mar 13 1922). The 1924 printing is a different printing and was never used as a source of text or page numbers.
pages_note: Article page numbers are the exact printed folios where the leafmap anchored them. Folios run continuously 1-3842 across the 7 article volumes. Volume 8 (study outlines and Fact-Index, folios 3843-4410) holds no articles; it is carried as a reference section (19 outline sections, 26 letter-history essays, 24,244 Fact-Index entries), kept separate from the article counts. Folio 1 occurs twice in vol. 1 (a portrait leaf and the text leaf 26, AACHEN); entries use the text pagination. No entry has a null page.
key_note: Keys are lowercase with non-alphanumerics stripped, as in the Britannica/Chambers's/Catholic/New International/Collier's/World Book builds. Leading digits are stripped from the KEY only (fused folio numbers); the display headword is kept verbatim. Headword stress apostrophes are kept as printed (e.g. AB'ELARD).
honest_limits: No second full-text copy exists: all verification was against this scan's own page images (HathiTrust is image-only; the 1924 printing is a different printing and was never used). Proofread coverage is partial everywhere (vol. 1: ~130 leaves read as images; vol. 2: 51/449 articles read; vol. 3: first 50 articles + every headword line; vol. 4: 50-article read; vol. 5: articles 100-149 + every headword line; vol. 6: every headword line + a contiguous run; vol. 7: 293 proofread fixes). A headword both merged mid-paragraph AND invisible to running heads could still be missed; the running-head audits found no further misses. Unrecovered items are listed per volume in unresolved.md (footer-bleed losses, picture-caption interleavings, garbled tokens left as-is, map/table/diagram labels). The book's own factual errors (e.g. URAL '16,000 miles', WALLACE 'Edward III') are kept as printed. PLATES: this site carries the full-page plate leaves (maps, portraits, full-page pictures) as web images, reduced in size for the web; small in-text figures are NOT included. Volume 8's gateway artwork appears twice: the frontispiece pair (leaves 1-2, the left half carrying the Library of Congress copyright-deposit label) and the end pair (leaves 579-580), both book-level plates with no article. GAP-FILL (2026-11-27): 18 articles the original parse had swept into neighbouring entries — 15 'Little Talks on Great Things' essays (AMBITION, CHIVALRY, COURAGE, EMOTIONS, FAITH, FRIENDSHIP, GOOD MANNERS, HUMILITY, IMAGINATION, KEEPING OUR WORD, OBEDIENCE, OPTIMISM, PURITY, SLANDER, THE VALUE OF TIME), PROTECTIVE COLORATION, LIFE-SAVING SERVICE and NATIONAL PARKS — were recovered from the same-edition leaf text, page images and the book's own Fact-Index and added; count 2,736 to 2,754. See work-sitebuild/gapfill-plates-report.md. NATIONAL PARKS' recovered text starts mid-sentence (its opening does not survive in the scan's OCR). VOLUME 8 (reference section, added 2026-11-27): 19 outline sections (181,656 words) as the printed Table of Contents lists them — Picture Story of Houses and Picture Story of Transportation are separate sections, not one; 26 letter-history essays (5,196 words), every one read from the page image; 24,244 Fact-Index entries as parsed (headword rows, exact count from the parse — the old 25,000-30,000 was a sampling estimate). Index entries are NOT articles and are kept separate from the 2,754 article count everywhere. Five entries are known false (continuation fragments, e.g. "Woodrow Wilson,") and are kept and flagged, not dropped; four real entries are known lost, their text preserved inside neighbouring entries (Joseph of Arimathe'a, Woolly bear, Nereus, Ural River). Subheadings inside long entries are sometimes split as separate rows, and table rows (coins, colleges, battles, sieges, popes) are absorbed into the preceding entry's text. Page references are heuristic (75,807 refs; a folio that coincides with a year can leak in or be dropped); 4,742 entries carry no refs. 2,195 index entries sit on the 44 interpolated folios (folio number interpolated from neighbours) and are flagged. The outlines' picture lists read left/right interleaved on 2-column leaves (all items present, order alternates). The LIST OF ABBREVIATIONS (551 pairs) and the copyright leaf are OCR-reconstructed, not image-verified. Full detail in vol8-report.md. AUDIT RESTORATIONS (2026-11-27): the no-omission audit found 4 passages where the cleanup had changed the printed text because the writer was judged wrong — BITTERSWEET 'Calastrus', ARMADA 'for . niggardly Queen Elizabeth', MOON 'that life has ever been upon the Moon', PATRICK, SAINT '(389?–461)' — all restored as printed, verified against the IA page images; and 9 article openings lost to the scan were restored from the same page images (PERCENTAGE AND INTEREST, PITCHER PLANTS, PUBLIC UTILITIES, RAPHAEL SANTI, RUSSIAN LITERATURE, SALVATION ARMY, SCHUMANN, ROBERT, TRENT, VICTORIA, Queen). See audit-restorations.md and work-sitebuild/audit-patches-log.md. One borderline case (APPLE 'NewBrunswick' vs 'New Brunswick') is still open for Larry to decide.
